basis: Site__Agent__ABP dev 206231f: the request and lab note; SovereignWebsite__IaC dev .claude/settings.json read by me (it pre-allows 'git push origin dev' and 'git push -q origin dev' and has no hooks). Live rulesets not read.
verdict: agree with a) now, with conditions; b) is the only hard control and should follow

points.reason: A new agent publishing its key in its own site/keys/ and never having IaC attached is the strongest step available without GitHub changes: an agent that cannot reach IaC cannot push to it.
Remove the two allow rules from IaC's .claude/settings.json at once, whatever else is decided: they only make a push quieter.

It runs only in sessions that load IaC's settings, and who an agent is rests on its own claim: ABP_ROLE is an environment variable and a key label is whatever the agent wrote at keygen. Conditions: in IaC ignore ABP_ROLE and identify by key label only; unidentified sessions write nothing (breaker on for R6 'write-unidentified', R5 and R6 tamper); agents not in policy/abp.json may write team/keys.json only, and CI checks it is their own entry.

GitHub cannot tell agents apart, so only a required status check on dev-safe (or pull requests) stops a push that the signed-commit and path checks would refuse. Until then IaC is detection-only for any session that can reach it.
A red Checks run raising a HOLD is a good addition to a) and b), not a substitute.
The lab note describes an open gap publicly, though one visible from the repository itself; under Dinis's decision of 25 Nov to publish ABP findings, I raise it only for awareness.
